analysis.title: GS Early Morning Research Recap: Ratings and Target Price Changes - November 10, 2026 as of 5:30 AM ET
key_insights: This is an index of Goldman Sachs research published through 5:30 AM ET on 10 Nov 2026. It lists rating changes, target price changes of 10% or more, notable stock notes by region, and upcoming webinars and conferences. Most entries are headlines only, so the stated views are limited to what the headlines say.

Three rating changes. Pluxee (PLX.PA) goes to Neutral from Sell after underperformance. Daikin Industries (6367.T) goes to Buy from Neutral on strong profit delivery. Kurita Water Industries (6370.T) goes to Neutral from Buy on uncertainty over electronics profit improvement. The Americas list has no rating changes.
Daikin's target rises to 30,000 yen from 26,000 yen, with the last price at 22,930 yen (31% upside). Kurita's target falls to 6,000 yen from 8,600 yen, with the last price at 5,388 yen (11% upside).

Americas target changes of 10% or more: Ionis (IONS, Neutral) to $41 from $58 with the last price at $31, Carlyle (CG, Buy) to $58 from $66 with the last price at $42.31, and H&R Block (HRB, Sell) to $40 from $36 with the last price at $50.98 (22% downside).
The Ionis note says it lowered its FY26 sHTG guidance, which the headline attributes to launch friction. The note awaits clarity on the trajectory.

H&R Block's F1Q note describes strategic progress, with assisted share improvement still to prove. The target is raised to $40 from $36 but stays well below the $50.98 last price, consistent with the Sell rating.

Asia target changes of 10% or more: Furukawa Electric (5801.T, Buy) to 4,100 yen from 6,400 yen despite a 2Q beat and a full-year guidance raise. Workman (7564.T, Neutral) to 6,000 yen from 6,800 yen. Denka (4061.T, Neutral) to 3,700 yen from 4,160 yen. Jiangsu King's Luck Brewery (603369.SS, Buy) to Rmb 37.60 from Rmb 33.00.

Three Asia Sell-rated names get new targets. Sinotrans (0598.HK) goes to HK$3.50 from HK$3.10, Yunda (002120.SZ) to Rmb 5.00 from Rmb 5.70, and China Resources Building Materials Tech (1313.HK) to HK$0.70 from HK$0.80.
Furukawa's headline says AI data center sentiment headwinds persist, but long-term agreements, including price revisions, raise visibility, and that corrected valuations are compelling.

China Data Center Electricals takeaways from the 800VDC Power & Cooling Corporate Day: no signs of demand slowdown so far, emerging ASIC opportunities, and a gradual 800 VDC transition. The note rates Kstar, Envicool, Hongfa and Jianghai Buy.

The Americas semiconductor note is titled as being at the center of tensions around the AI datacenter build and searches for value after a sector-wide pullback. Europe datacenter research says the growth path is solid and unaffected by the US midterms.

Macro and strategy notes listed: US Economics Analyst 2027 Consumer Outlook (Steady Through the Shocks), Global Rates Notes on reserves in an ample liquidity regime, and a US Daily October CPI Preview dated 9 Nov. A CPI First-Take webinar is scheduled for 9:45 AM ET today, so the print is due today. No figures from these notes appear in the recap.

Strategy notes: GOAL Kickstart on tracking rotations across AI and markets after the midterms, Global Weekly Kickstart on Europe taking a different route to AI, and an Asian equity market daily update.

Earnings-season takeaways in Americas headlines: Mattel (MAT) reduces estimates on lowered 2026 guidance. Optimum Communications (OPTU) missed on EBITDA, with continued broadband weakness and higher expenses. Take-Two (TTWO) reiterated its FY27 bookings outlook with focus on the GTA VI launch.

More Americas earnings headlines: BitGo (BTGO) shows continued institutional client growth against weaker operating results. ZipRecruiter (ZIP) shows accelerating growth from marketplace improvements. Zeta Global (ZETA) cites AI adoption contributing to growth acceleration. Onto Innovation (ONTO) reports a strong quarter and guidance with advanced packaging momentum into 2027.

Rockwell Automation (ROK) gets raised estimates despite moderating growth. CF Industries, Mosaic and Nutrien each get estimate revisions after Q3 results. Entegris (ENTG) held a Capital Markets Day that laid out a long-term model. O'Reilly (ORLY, Buy, on the Conviction List) has takeaways from a virtual group meeting with its CFO.

Europe: CNH Industrial (CNH) 3Q26 is described as mixed excluding refunds, with consensus EPS likely mechanically up high-single-digit. CNH also announced the divestment of its Construction Equipment business. Teleperformance's topline inflection is delayed further (Neutral). Enagas keeps a Sell on structural headwinds that still outweigh the positives.

Asia: Denka had a 2Q beat with FY guidance raised, but higher fixed costs and fading inventory gains weigh (Neutral). Chiba Bank's upward revisions reflect a policy rate hike from 0.75% to 1.25% and it announced a share buyback. Amcor lowered its transition period guide, with CY27 execution key (Buy). Monadelphous keeps a Sell because valuation appears full.

Americas industry and sector data headlines: Illinois gaming revenue +10% y/y in October, Ohio racinos +6% y/y, the GS Housing Market Activity Scale down 2% sequentially for the week of November 1, and the GS Supply Chain Congestion Scale index lower w/w with the bottleneck scale unchanged at 2.

LatAm: GAP (GAPB.MX) October traffic -7% YoY, LATAM Airlines (LTM) October capacity/demand +8% YoY, Ecorodovias October traffic -3% YoY. Grupo SBF and TIM Brasil results were broadly in line. Magazine Luiza was in line with a marked pick-up in sales growth into early 4Q.

China consumer and auto data: weekly NEV orders were -25% wow and -18% yoy, with NEV/ICE dealer discounts widened. The China Property weekly wrap says transaction activity broadly softened, consistent with seasonality. The China Spirits Tracker says high-end wholesale prices stay soft.

Scheduled events: Beauty Update at 10 AM ET today. On November 12: Arjun Murti fireside at 9 AM ET, then the 2027 Global Economics Outlook (12 PM), Markets Outlook (12:35 PM), Strategy Outlook (1:10 PM) and Commodities Outlook (1:45 PM), a US Data Center Power call at 7:30 PM ET, and a China property call at 10 PM ET. A Jet Fuel call is on November 13 at 8 AM ET.

Recent podcast and replay titles show current client topics: US midterm first take, midterm implications for green energy and utilities in Europe, Middle East escalation risks after the midterms, the Israel election, and the UK Budget.

earnings_insights: Ionis (IONS) lowered FY26 sHTG guidance, which GS attributes to launch friction. Target cut to $41 from $58, Neutral. No figures for the guidance are given in this recap.
Mattel (MAT): GS reduces estimates on lowered 2026 guidance, with new leadership refocusing on the core toy business. Reported results are not quantified in this recap.
Optimum Communications (OPTU) 3Q26: EBITDA miss on continued broadband weakness and higher expenses. The size of the miss and the comparison basis are not given.
Take-Two (TTWO) FQ2'27: FY27 bookings outlook reiterated. GS says focus remains on the GTA VI launch.
BitGo (BTGO) 3Q26 EPS: continued institutional client growth versus weaker operating results. No EPS figure is given.

ZipRecruiter (ZIP) Q3'26: marketplace improvements drive accelerating growth. Zeta Global (ZETA) 3Q26: AI adoption contributes to growth acceleration. Onto Innovation (ONTO): strong quarter and guidance, with advanced packaging momentum continuing into 2027.
Rockwell Automation (ROK): estimates raised despite moderating growth. CF Industries (CF), Mosaic (MOS) and Nutrien (NTR): estimates revised after Q3 results. No figures are given.
CNH Industrial (CNH) 3Q26 mixed excluding refunds. GS says consensus EPS is likely mechanically up high-single-digit. This is a consensus estimate, not a reported print.

Denka (4061.T) 2Q beat, driven by AI-related materials, with FY guidance raised. Higher fixed costs and fading inventory gains weigh. Furukawa Electric (5801.T) 2Q beat and full-year guidance raise. Kikkoman (2801.T) 2Q beat and full-year guidance hike, with focus on the timing of North America price hikes.

Namura Shipbuilding (7014.T): profits below GSe but within the volatility range, with full-year guidance and DPS raised. Softbank Corp. (9434.T): results and new guidance in line, 2H profit growth to accelerate.

Chiba Bank (8331.T) 2Q in line. Upward revisions reflect a policy rate hike from 0.75% to 1.25%, and the bank announced a share buyback. Amcor (AMC.AX): transition period guide lowered. ANZ Group (ANZ.AX) FY26 result review: shifting into a year of consolidation.

LatAm 3Q26: Grupo SBF in line with softer sales and operating deleverage. TIM Brasil broadly in line, with MSR growth deceleration already expected by consensus. Magazine Luiza broadly in line with a marked pick-up in sales growth into early 4Q.
Asset manager 3Q26 EPS wrap-ups cover KKR and AMG, and CY3Q26 wrap-ups cover BAM, BEN, CG, NTRS, STEP, VCTR and VIRT. The recap gives no figures.
